LAREDO, Texas — United ISD leaders, trustees, staff, and project partners celebrated the grand opening of the district’s new state-of-the-art Child Nutrition Center this week — a project more than a decade in the making that was built without using district construction funds, according to United ISD.

The 58,000-square-foot facility supports the preparation and distribution of approximately 55,000 meals daily — breakfast, lunch, snacks, and supper — for nearly 39,000 students across the district.

The project’s origins trace back to 2014, when district leadership learned that the planned expansion of East Loop 20 would directly impact the former Child Nutrition Center. Rather than simply replacing the building, UISD leadership, legal counsel, and state officials negotiated with the Texas Department of Transportation to secure a modern facility while protecting uninterrupted meal services.

Board Vice President Aliza Flores-Oliveros called the grand opening “the biggest achievement in her decade of service on the Board,” recalling how, as a young board member, she questioned why the center had to be torn down. Former Superintendent Roberto Santos, who led the district when the effort began and assured the board the negotiation would pay off, attended the ribbon-cutting ceremony.

Board President Javier Montemayor credited productive, transparent negotiations with state leaders, saying they were “very cooperative and very helpful” and recognized the facility’s essential role. Project legal counsel Eddie Vassallo of Vassallo & Salazar Attorneys at Law said the outcome was “a cooperative effort between the state and UISD to build something that is for the benefit of the students of UISD and something that will serve this district for decades to come.”

Superintendent Dr. Gerardo Cruz said the center’s true value rests in the children it feeds each day, noting the district focuses on students’ nutritional well-being alongside academics, and praised the child nutrition staff as “second to none.”

Following the ribbon-cutting, guests toured the facility, which features a cook-chill system able to produce thousands of meals daily, a bakery, large dry storage, freezers, and student instructional areas. Project partners included Leyendecker Construction of Texas, Able City, and Vassallo & Salazar Attorneys at Law.

Sources:
